To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the research has demonstrated how drawing, as a way of coming to knowledge, can be used to explicate the “lived experiences” of a subject.
Drawing, as a way of knowing, can be used to explore and explicate the complexities of experience and its interpretation.
Drawing, as a means to explicate experience, is an integral part of the creative process and the creative process is integral to the explication of experience.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of what it means to draw, how we draw and why we draw.
the relationship between the body and the world, and the role of drawing in the articulation of the body as an integral part of the world.
the relationship between perception, ideation and praxis, and the role of the lived experience of the artist in the development of their practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the research is an investigation into the “lived ex- perience” through drawing.

the research has provided an understanding of the relationship between drawing and perception, and the role that this relationship has on the “lived experi- ence”, and that this has been articulated in the form of a thesis.
drawing is an integral part of the lived experience, it is a process that is inextricably linked to the body, to the mind, and to the environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the research has provided a way of understanding how drawing can provide a means of explicating and articulating experience, as a form of knowledge.
we have developed an approach for investigating the role of drawing as a means for understanding the world, and ourselves, as we engage in it.
the “lived” experience is a process of being and becoming.
The main takeaway from our work is that
drawing, as a practice, is an integral part of the process of knowing, and that it is through the act of drawing that we can come to understand our “lived experience”.
the “lived experiences” (Dilthe, 2002) are the basis of the “lifework” and “lifework” can be seen as a way to understand the “lifeworld”.
